I am an atheist in the strongest sense attainable without abandoning rationality; I don't claim complete certainty, as I understand the impossibility of disproving an unfalsifiable claim. But my disbelief in deities is as strong as rational disbelief gets.

Ask me anything and receive a reasonable, evidence-based reply!
IAMA I am a reasonable and well-educated atheist.

I don't hate America. I disapprove of some things that the American government does, and of some things that some American people do.

But how could I hate America? America is an abstraction with no particular existence except as a useful shorthand. I'm only capable of hating things that have some meaningful existence.
So are you just looking for an excuse to argue with someone, or what?

Not really; I made this in reaction to another active thread, in which a strong atheist is attempting to argue their views (which are quite irrational).

Why do you hate God? . . . Just Kidding, fellow atheist here. If you were raised religious, how did you go about letting your family know?

I've actually got a younger sister who's being raised religious in my family, and it's sad to see her blindly follow without much question. Do you have any siblings being raised religious? If so, how's your relationship with them if you're out?

Why do you hate God?

Haha - I refer you to my answer re hating America: "[I don't]; I'm only capable of hating things that have some meaningful existence."

If you were raised religious, how did you go about letting your family know?

I was not raised religious; one of my parents was a disinterested agnostic, and the other a progressive Christian with a somewhat confused and inconstant faith. We sometimes went to Church, but it came and went in phases, and was not part of my life past middle childhood.

That said, it took a long time for me to be comfortable coming out as an atheist to my Christian parent. I am quite open about it now, and readily bring up my views when that parent brings up religious topics. But it's always uncomfortable for them, and so I tend to avoid the subject. I don't recall exactly when or how I came out; I believe it was a gradual introduction of more and more atheistic views (I never endorsed theistic views, but didn't come on strong with straight atheism right away either).

I find childhood indoctrination very disturbing. If I knew that someone in my family was being raised with religious views, I would do my best to undermine that - even at the expense of relations with a sibling or whatever.
